rationale: Calls frappe.rate_limiter Python module directly, never over HTTP; ferro has no rate-limiter subsystem and relies on upstream infra (Caddy/nginx) for that concern.
Tests the Python Rating field clamp logic inside frappe.new_doc/insert; ferro does not reimplement field-type coercion and this is pure in-process Python validation.
frappe.recorder is a Python dev-mode profiling tool that hooks into frappe.db; ferro does not implement this subsystem and it is never exercised over HTTP.
Tests the @frappe.recorder.record_queries decorator — pure Python dev-tooling, not part of ferro's scope.
Tests the normalize_query() Python utility function used by the recorder; pure string-processing with no HTTP interaction and no ferro equivalent.

sub_area: Redis ACL user management for RQ queue isolation
rationale: Tests Redis ACL provisioning for RQ workers; ferro replaces Redis with an in-process cache/queue and has no equivalent ACL management surface.
Tests frappe.model.sync.remove_orphan_entities, a developer-mode file-system sync tool; ferro does not implement module/fixture sync logic.

sub_area: Document rename/merge (frappe.rename_doc, bulk_rename, autoincrement docs, child-table parenttype fix-up)
rationale: frappe.rename_doc is a complex Python operation (link-field rewriting, controller renaming, DDL) that ferro does not reimplement; any rename support would require ferrod Python fallthrough.

sub_area: Report view CSV export and field-name extraction utility
rationale: export_query() and extract_fieldnames() are part of the Python report/export subsystem; ferro intentionally does not implement report export pipelines.
safe_exec is the server-script Python sandbox; ferro does not execute server scripts and has no safe_exec equivalent.

sub_area: ServerScriptNotEnabled guard when safe_exec is disabled
rationale: Tests that safe_exec raises ServerScriptNotEnabled by default; purely Python, not relevant to ferro.

sub_area: Jinja environment thread-safety and restrict_globals injection
rationale: Tests Jinja2 template environment setup; ferro uses Rust-side HTML rendering and does not use Frappe's Python Jinja globals.

sub_area: Python scheduler: enqueue_events, dormant-site detection, sleep alignment
rationale: Tests the Python RQ-based scheduler (enqueue_events, is_dormant, schedule_jobs_based_on_activity); ferro replaces this with an in-process Rust scheduler and does not share the Python scheduler API.

sub_area: Desk link-search and search_widget (search_link, search_widget, user-permission filtering, SQL injection sanitization)
rationale: search_link/search_widget are whitelisted desk methods (frappe.desk.search.*) that ferro's desk.rs partially reimplements; the permission-aware query logic and SQL injection guards encode behaviors ferro must match, but the test calls Python directly, not HTTP.

sub_area: _seen field tracking (getdoc marks document as seen per user)
rationale: _seen is a Frappe Desk collaboration feature maintained by the Python getdoc hook; ferro's desk.rs loads documents but does not implement _seen tracking.

sub_area: Sentry scope enrichment for RQ background jobs (wait-time calculation)
rationale: Tests frappe.utils.sentry.set_scope for RQ job telemetry; this is observability tooling for the Python worker, entirely outside ferro's scope.
